rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The **What happened:** block is OPTIONAL -- default is to omit it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 89: "**What happened:** A one-screen gap map across memory / verifier / skill, one stale rule cut in place, and a diagrammed map of the work that recurs across your stack. The shapes feed the handoff prompt you write in the close." Inclusion test met: three artefacts (gap map, rule cut, stack diagram) land across two phases with no single slide carrying all three -- the rule's own bar for keeping the block. Move 1 (count + noun, artefact as grammatical subject): satisfied by the compound subject itself -- "A one-screen gap map", "one stale rule cut in place", "a diagrammed map" -- numerals doing the naming work the rule asks for, extended to three artefacts the way the rule's own example "One plan, two reads" already compounds. Move 2 (one qualifier on what makes it yours, not how you got it): "across your stack" ties the diagrammed map to the student's own work, not to method -- this is the harm rule 16 exists to prevent (a recap that reads as generic instruction-replay rather than the student's own artefact), and it is absent here. Move 3 (land on the destination): "The shapes feed the handoff prompt you write in the close" names both what reads it next (the handoff prompt) and where (the close) -- this is the exact fix for the prior REVISE, which flagged "The shapes carry into the close" as passive and vague. The new clause names an actor (the shapes), a concrete destination (the handoff prompt), and a location (the close) -- no longer passive, no longer vague. 2 sentences, 37 words, inside the rule's 1-3 sentence / 25-40 word band.

notes: The '**What happened:**' block at line 89 is NOT the file's last body content -- '## Decide what crosses back to your main repo' follows it (lines 91-93), before the maintainer cut at line 95. Rule 16's move-3 destination language ('land on the destination... points forward') implicitly assumes this block is the exercise's terminal beat; here it is a mid-body Phase-2 recap with one more section after it. This did not change my verdict -- the block still passes its own three-move test on its own terms, and the maintainer's stated inclusion rationale (three artefacts, two phases, no single slide carries all three) is a Phase-recap justification, not a closer justification, so the rule's intent (don't let a recap replay steps or drift) still applies and still holds. But this looks like a rule-fit question worth flagging: rule 16 as written reads as though it always sits at the exercise's true end, and this instance breaks that assumption cleanly. Recommend the maintainer either broaden rule 16's framing to cover mid-body multi-artefact recaps explicitly, or confirm the current text already covers it (the 'Standard shape' language never says 'must be last'). Not filed as a rule_evaluated finding since it is a question about the rule's scope, not a body violation -- per dispatch-preamble guidance to route rule questions to notes rather than REVISE when the obvious fix would degrade nothing but the rule's own precision needs maintainer judgment.
